transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brought me in is that I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'm a software developer, and lately... I'll be in the middle of fixing a rendering bug, and something like a Slack ping, or a color pattern on the screen, or even a siren outside will just completely derail me. It pulls me into a whole new idea before I can even finish typing the line of code. It's getting really hard to work like this.
Besides the trouble focusing, have you noticed that you're fidgeting a lot, feeling restless, or acting on impulses without thinking them through?

I wouldn't say I'm fidgeting, really. It's more like... I just have so much I need to get done right now. I've been working on this huge new project on the side, and it's kind of taken over. I've been emailing art curators, pitching community leaders, completely rewriting the backend of the software... I'm even mock-planning these big physical installations. I'm trying to recruit other developers to help me, too, texting them at all hours. It just feels so much bigger and more important than my regular job right now, so I have to keep moving on it.

Over this past period when you've been working intensely on this project, how has your mood been? Would you say you've been feeling unusually happy, excited, or like everything is possible—more so than is typical for you?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. Most days lately, I just feel... lit up. Unstoppable, really. It's like the whole city of Glendale has finally caught up to the frequency of what I'm building, and everything just makes sense. I feel fantastic. But... well, I do get pretty short with people. If my wife asks me to stop and explain things, or if my coworkers try to slow me down with their, you know, "process" and red tape, I snap at them. Hard. It's just frustrating when people can't see the vision and they just get in the way. But overall, yeah, I feel incredible.
Have you ever had a period—maybe weeks or months—where you felt the opposite: really down, hopeless, like nothing mattered, and you couldn't get out of bed or do your normal activities?

No, I can't really say that I have. I mean, sure, I get stressed out sometimes—like if a software release isn't going well or something—but... feeling hopeless or not being able to get out of bed? No. I haven't experienced anything like that. I usually always have some project or something driving me forward, so I've never really had a period where I just shut down like you're describing.
How long has this period of feeling 'lit up' and working intensely on this project been going on? Has it been days, weeks, or longer?

It's been going on for... I'd say about three months now. Yeah, right around three months. That's when my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase, and ever since then, I've just been completely dialed into it.

Before this three-month period started, going back over your entire life, have you ever had another time—even if it was brief—where you felt this same kind of 'lit up' energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, or heightened productivity?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been pretty driven with my work, and sure, I've pulled a late night here or there to finish a software build. But... no, nothing like this. 

This specific feeling, being this energized and just completely dialed in for months... this is the first time I've ever experienced anything on this level. So, no, I haven't had a time like this in the past.
